Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • To group content that belongs together and sits on the page: a summary, a panel of settings, one item in a grid.
  • As the surface of a tile that opens something, with the interactive variant.
  • To hold rows or sections that run edge to edge, with the flush variant.
  • To mark a slot that is still empty and invite the first item, with the empty variant.

When not to use

  • For a whole page band or section background: use the layout foundation's sections (ds-section--sunken, ds-section--raised).
  • To frame a single line of text or one control; let space do the grouping.
  • For a message about a problem or result: use cmp-inline-alert.
  • Inside another card. Nest sections in a flush card instead.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

  • plain — a raised surface with a hairline edge, a soft shadow and inner padding. The default: the base class alone, no modifier class.
  • interactive — the whole card is one link or button (a tile): it lifts and its shadow deepens on hover.
  • flush — no inner padding, so rows, images and __body sections run edge to edge; each __body brings its own padding and a divider between sections.
  • empty — a dashed outline on no fill, for something not made yet: an empty slot or a planned item. It holds a short line and at most one action.

Anatomy

  • Root: <div class="ds-card">; an <a class="ds-card ds-card--interactive"> or <button> when the whole card acts; <section> or <article> when it has its own heading. Combine --interactive with --flush for tiles with a picture area.
  • Title (optional): <h3 class="ds-card__title"> (or the heading level the page needs), first in the card.
  • Text: paragraphs and other foundation-styled content inside the card.
  • Meta (optional): <p class="ds-card__meta"> for secondary facts (owner, date, count), muted and small.
  • Body (flush only): <div class="ds-card__body">, one per padded section.

Accessibility

  • A card that acts is a single <a href> or <button> with a clear accessible name, usually its title; it contains no other links or buttons.
  • A card with its own heading uses a real heading element at the right level, so the card can be found by heading navigation.
  • Grouping is visual only; use section with a heading or aria-labelledby when the group needs a name for assistive technology.
  • Focus on an acting card draws the shared ring around the whole card.

Interaction

  • An interactive card lifts by the motion lift over the settling duration and its edge darkens on hover; a link or button card that is not interactive only darkens its edge (int-01, int-04).
  • Focus is always visible on cards that act, and stays on the card after it opens something in place (int-02).
  • Pressing an interactive card never changes its size; under reduced motion the lift is off (int-03, int-06).

Content rules

  • Titles are short and specific, in sentence case: "Weekly review", not "Card title" or "Item".
  • One idea per card; if a card needs a scroll bar, it is a page.
  • Meta lines put the most useful fact first: "Updated 2 days ago · 4 people".
  • Empty cards say what is missing and the one way to add it: "No people yet. Add the first person."

Do and don't

  • Do align cards on the layout grid and keep the cards in one row the same height.
  • Do use the flush variant for lists of rows inside a card, so row highlights reach the edges.
  • Don't put a card inside a card, or give a card a coloured background.
  • Don't make only part of an interactive card clickable.
